rules: All neural-network fitting and scalar clustering require CUDA; no CPU fallback. Hungarian alignment and reporting may use CPU.
Teacher: 32 inputs, 16 tanh hidden units, zero fixed biases, fixed readout 1/4. All solvers have exactly this architecture.
Every bank has a new balanced random assignment of 512 weights to 32 codes. Source tasks have exact sharing and independent Uniform[-1,1] codebooks.

Extract the indexator from fitted dense source weights: GPU scalar k-means, Hungarian hidden-unit alignment by equality signatures, code-label alignment, vote across the best fit per source task. Teacher comparisons occur only after extraction.

Within each bank, calibration or evaluation tasks add Gaussian weight residuals orthogonal to the true base-sharing space. The residual Frobenius norm equals the stated ratio times the base-weight norm. Tasks and datasets are independent of source fitting; conditions share base codes, residual directions and inputs for pairing.
No target tasks are generated until global learning rates have been frozen using the two calibration banks. No evaluation bank or target outcome may change this protocol or selection.
Raw SGDM sums gradients within a group. Normalized SGDM averages them, exactly implementing momentum in orthonormal sharing coordinates while the partition is fixed.

Adaptive splits maximize squared gradient contrast by sorting within each current group. All splits at an event use the full support gradient already computed for that update. This is an empirical direction heuristic, not the independently confirmed population-noise theorem.

At a split copy the old code and its physical-coordinate momentum into both children, preserving the represented function and the old momentum direction. The new contrast starts with zero momentum. Dense and fixed controls retain their ordinary uninterrupted optimizer state.

Random control replays adaptive parent-group labels and child sizes at each event, then assigns positions randomly within its own corresponding parent. This matches K and every group size for each task/start/step; it even retains adaptive information about which group to split.

All methods use four starts, 4096 full-support gradient steps and the same checkpoint schedule. Split search consumes no additional labels or backward passes; wall-clock overhead is reported separately, so equal steps are not claimed to mean equal FLOPs or time.

Each method has five learning-rate candidates. A common normalized rate minimizes mean calibration query NMSE across fixed_normalized, adaptive and random_matched, averaging conditions and banks after selecting the best start/checkpoint. Raw, dense SGDM and dense Adam select their own rates.
Validation selects checkpoints and starts. Main output includes both selection across all K and selection within fixed-K phases, especially K=96, so the matched-complexity comparison is explicit.

128 examples are used for gradients and 1024 additional labels for validation; do not describe 128 as the total labeled-data budget. Held-out 8192-example errors are evaluated only after model selection.

Save source and target train/query loss curves, auxiliary positive-sign recall, gradient-conflict energy, K, split decisions, all checkpoint-selection outcomes, numeric models and frozen hashes. Positive-sign recall is auxiliary for this regression task.

Aggregate independent evaluation banks first; paired task differences within a bank are not independent bank replications. This is a small mechanism pilot, not a general MLP theorem or a comparison proving necessity of an AR generator.
No tests are added or run. Preserve all other repository changes. Do not commit or push this experiment without a new instruction.
